reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that speech functions as an instrumental tool, enabling causal transfer across agents without direct physical intervention. In mathematical terms, this can be modeled as a functional transformation where the speaker's internal state (C) maps to a desired external behavior (B) in the listener. The tool-like nature implies a structured interface: T_s manipulates T_l to produce B. This is formalized through a causal operator T such that T(C) = B. For commands, the operator is deterministic under ideal conditions; for proclamations, it introduces probabilistic elements due to mental model alignment. Failure modes arise when either the tool (T) is misapplied or the agent states (A_s, A_l) are incompatible. The system exhibits duality: commands are direct action-inducers while proclamations are indirect belief-inducers. Both rely on shared symbolic structures and mutual understanding. The breakdown occurs when the speaker’s means-end capacities fall short of the required manipulation or when the listener cannot decode the intended action.
